definition.def: To advance means to move forward, often in order to attack someone.
examples: The Allies began advancing on the city in 1943. [VERB preposition/adverb]
The water is advancing at a rate of 5cm a day. [VERB]
...a picture of a man throwing himself before an advancing tank. [VERB-ing]

definition.def: To advance means to make progress, especially in your knowledge of something.
examples: Medical technology has advanced considerably. [VERB]

definition.def: If you advance someone a sum of money, you lend it to them, or pay it to them earlier than arranged.
examples: I advanced him some money, which he would repay on our way home. [VERB noun noun]
The bank advanced $1.2 billion to help the country with debt repayments. [VERB noun]

definition.def: An advance is money which is lent or paid to someone before they would normally receive it.
examples: She was paid a £100,000 advance for her next two novels.

definition.def: To advance an event, or the time or date of an event, means to bring it forward to an earlier time or date.
examples: Too much protein in the diet may advance the ageing process. [VERB noun]
The country's election commission has advanced the date of the election by three days. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you advance a cause, interest, or claim, you support it and help to make it successful.
examples: When not producing art of his own, Oliver was busy advancing the work of others. [VERB noun]

definition.def: When a theory or argument is advanced, it is put forward for discussion.
examples: Many theories have been advanced as to why some women suffer from depression. [be VERB-ed]
An explanation has now been advanced by scientists.  [be VERB-ed]

definition.def: An advance is a forward movement of people or vehicles, usually as part of a military operation.
examples: ...an advance on enemy positions. [+ on]
The defences are intended to obstruct any advance by tanks and other vehicles.

definition.def: If you make advances to someone, you try to start a sexual relationship with them. [old-fashioned]
examples: Mark had for some time been making advances towards her.
She rejected his advances during the trip to Cannes.

definition.def: An advance in a particular subject or activity is progress in understanding it or in doing it well.
examples: ...the technological advances of the last four decades.
Their progress at work was mirrored by their children's educational advance.

definition.def: If something is an advance on what was previously available or done, it is better in some way.
examples: This could be an advance on the present situation. [+ on]

definition.def: Advance booking, notice, or warning is done or given before an event happens.
examples: They don't normally give any advance notice about which building they're going to inspect.
The event received little advance publicity.

definition.def: An advance party or group is a small group of people who go on ahead of the main group.
examples: The 20-strong advance party will be followed by another 600 soldiers.

definition.def: If one thing happens or is done in advance of another, it happens or is done before the other thing.
examples: I had asked everyone to submit questions in advance of the meeting.

definition.def: If you do something in advance, you do it before a particular date or event.
examples: The subject of the talk is announced a week in advance.

examples.sentence: Fear, for example, can limit the development of curiosity, which is a strong force in scientific advance, because it motivates problem-solving behaviour.
Birds will fatten themselves with heavy feeding in advance of a long migrational flight.
he or she would have needed to know in advance how to find the location of the true opening in the wall.
The Step Pyramid was a revolutionary advance in architecture and became the archetype which all the other great pyramid builders of Egypt would follow.
Other species, such as daffodils, have considerable temperature sensitivity, and can flower months in advance during a warm winter.
Construction marks left on a Roman tunnel in Bologna show that the rate of advance through solid rock was 30 centimeters per day.
In contrast, the rate of advance of the Claudius tunnel can be calculated at 1.4 meters per day.

He was not active (with a few exceptions) in scientific societies, and did not seek to find influence or advance his ideas through professional contacts and politics, spending most of his time at home in his study reading and writing, or in the field collecting observations.

In June 1992 political and environmental leaders from across the world met in Rio de Janeiro to discuss how developing countries can advance their economies without destroying their natural resources.

The government needs to create sustainable, competitive and diverse farming and food sectors, which will contribute to a thriving and sustainable rural economy, and advance environmental, economic, health, and animal welfare goals.
